                    ### Question
                    An otherwise healthy 16-year-old girl comes to the physician because she has not had a menstrual period. Examination shows normal breast development. There is coarse pubic and axillary hair. Pelvic examination shows a blind vaginal pouch. Ultrasonography shows normal ovaries and an atretic uterus. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Deficiency of 5-alpha reductase
opb. End-organ insensitivity to androgens
opc. Monosomy of sex chromosomes
opd. Agenesis of the paramesonephric duct
ope. Deficiency of 17-alpha-hydroxylase

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient presents with primary amenorrhea, normal breast development indicating estrogen presence, and coarse pubic and axillary hair suggesting androgen activity. The pelvic examination reveals a blind vaginal pouch and ultrasonography shows normal ovaries and an atretic uterus, indicating a failure of Müllerian duct development. This aligns with the diagnosis of agenesis of the paramesonephric duct (Müllerian agenesis), which is the most likely underlying cause of her symptoms. Other options, such as deficiency of 5-alpha reductase, end-organ insensitivity to androgens, monosomy of sex chromosomes, and deficiency of 17-alpha-hydroxylase, do not fit the clinical picture as they would present with different findings or hormonal profiles.
